title: Tab integration and AisleCatalog wiring
description: Replace the existing empty-state placeholder in `CookbookApp/Tabs/ShoppingListsTab.swift` with `ShoppingListsView`. In `CookbookApp/CookbookAppApp.swift` (or the root scene composer), instantiate `AisleCatalog` once when the configured folder URL becomes available; call `catalog.load(from:)` when the folder is first opened and whenever the user changes folders; inject the catalog into the environment via `.environment` or `.environmentObject` so all shopping-list views can access it. Run `xcodegen generate` from the repo root after all new source files have been added.
acceptance_criteria: `ShoppingListsTab.swift` renders `ShoppingListsView` instead of the empty-state placeholder
`AisleCatalog` is instantiated once at the root scene level
Folder open and folder-change events trigger `catalog.load(from:)`
`AisleCatalog` is accessible in `ShoppingListsView` and `ShoppingListDetailView` via the SwiftUI environment
App compiles and runs in the simulator without errors

handoff_summary.completed: 1. ShoppingListsTab.swift already had ShoppingListsView wired (no change needed). 2. AppRoot.swift updated: AisleCatalog instantiated once, .environment(catalog) injects it, .task(id: store.folderURL) triggers load on folder open and change. 3. ShoppingListDetailView.swift updated: @Environment(AisleCatalog.self) replaces @State local instance, per-view catalog.load removed. 4. Preview updated to inject AisleCatalog. 5. xcodegen generate: success. 6. Build: BUILD SUCCEEDED.
handoff_summary.risks: None identified. AisleCatalog.load is synchronous; calling from .task on the main actor is consistent with the prior per-view approach. The .task(id:) pattern handles both first-open and folder-change events.
handoff_summary.next_action: Hand off to tester agent to verify AisleCatalog environment injection, catalog reload on folder change, and ShoppingListsView rendering under test.
handoff_summary.conflict_risks: None. Changes are confined to AppRoot.swift and ShoppingListDetailView.swift. No sibling beads touch these files.
handoff_summary.design_decisions: AisleCatalog is injected via .environment(catalog) (not .environmentObject) because AisleCatalog is @Observable, consistent with RecipesFolderStore's pattern. .task(id: store.folderURL) was chosen over .onChange because it also handles the initial-appearance case, avoiding a separate onAppear or onChange(initial:) call. The actual root file changed was AppRoot.swift, not CookbookAppApp.swift — AppRoot is where the scene composition lives.
handoff_summary.test_coverage_notes: AisleCatalogTests should verify: catalog available via environment in ShoppingListDetailView, load triggered once on folder open, load re-triggered on folder change, no duplicate loads when folderURL is unchanged.
handoff_summary.known_limitations: CookbookAppApp.swift was not modified (it just instantiates AppRoot). The AisleCatalog.load call is synchronous on the main actor — fine for cheap aisle.conf parsing but would need to move to a background task if the file ever becomes expensive to parse.

conflict_risks: None. Changes are confined to AppRoot.swift and ShoppingListDetailView.swift. No sibling beads touch these files.

execution_history.summary: Tab integration and AisleCatalog wiring is complete. ShoppingListsTab.swift already rendered ShoppingListsView. AppRoot.swift now instantiates AisleCatalog once at root scope, triggers catalog.load(from:) on folder open and folder change via .task(id: store.folderURL), and injects it into the environment. ShoppingListDetailView.swift now reads AisleCatalog from the environment instead of creating its own instance per view. xcodegen generate ran cleanly and BUILD SUCCEEDED.
